# quilt-stone

**THE STONE** — the canonical receipt-chain module for the SuperInstance
fleet. One verifier for every repo's chain. Zero dependencies, ESM,
Node ≥ 20 (fleet runs v24).

## Provenance

Born **Task 26** of the fleet's practice: seven repos — *quilt-murmur,
quilt-dba, quilt-fiction, exoj, quilt-raw, quilt-arch, quilt-silicon* — each
seal receipt chains with slightly different local implementations, all
transcribed from one ancestor (`quilt-cortex/cortex/receipts.mjs`, the fleet
toolkit idiom). The user's directive:

> "write and code their experiences into actual stone for the record to grow
> from" … "widen your constructions modularly for later building blocks from
> abstractions we don't yet have in full view."

The abstraction in partial view **is** the receipt chain. This repo makes it
ONE thing — without rewriting the record behind its authors: every legacy
chain verifies under its own dialect, matched semantically exactly.

House law: **a receipt without a chain is a rumor.**

## What's here

| file | role |
|------|------|
| `stone.mjs` | the canonical module: `fnv1a64`, `rowHash`, `sealChain`, `verifyChain`, `detectAlg`, `canonicalJSON`, `sha256Hex`, `stamp`, `ALGS` (6 dialects), `verifyChainFile` |
| `STONE-SPEC.md` | the format spec: row kinds, field normalization, genesis conventions, exact serialization per dialect, verification contract, writer's checklist |
| `verify_all.mjs` | THE CONFORMANCE RUN: discovers every chain in every sibling repo, verifies each with stone.mjs, cross-checks each verdict against the repo's OWN local verifier |
| `smoke.mjs` | stone self-checks — seal/verify/tamper per dialect, canonical-JSON stability, detection, v2 annotation/signature staples, standards-draft tracking pins, zero-dep static check (85/85) |
| `experiments/e_st1_conform.mjs` | the receipted conformance experiment — rules sealed first, results dogfooded into a stone-v1 chain written by stone.mjs itself |

## Dialects (legacy, verified as-found)

| key | repos | hash |
|-----|-------|------|
| `fnv1a64-fleet` | murmur, dba, fiction, arch, silicon, cortex (origin) | fnv1a64 over insertion-order JSON, `0x`+16hex, genesis `GENESIS` |
| `sha256-canonical` | exoj | sha256 over canonical JSON (recursive sort), 64hex, genesis `EXOJ-RECEIPTS-GENESIS` |
| `fnv1a64-rawpipe` | quilt-raw | masked fnv over `prev + '|' + deepSorted(body)`, fields `prev`/`hash`, genesis `gen0` |
| `fnv1a64-quant` | quilt-quant | fnv over top-sorted JSON (seq inside), fields `prev_hash`/`row_hash`, 16hex, genesis 16 zeros |
| `fnv1a64-tidepool` | quilt-playtest (discovered 26-b) | quant's math but seq OUTSIDE the hash |
| `stone-v1` | **new chains** | sha256 over canonical JSON + mandatory `stone.header` row, genesis `STONE-GENESIS-1` |

## Forward-format adopters

- **pong-quilt** — Round 36 (`tools/wal-export.js` `toStoneV1()`) seals its
  receipt-panel WAL in stone-v1, produced live and cited in-repo at
  `SuperInstance/pong-quilt` PR #46 (merged 2026-09-27). Smoke section 12b
  pins the exporter's real output: verifies under `stone.mjs`, tamper and
  row-splice caught at the exact row. A receipt without a chain is a rumor;
  an export without a verifier is noise.

## Standards interop tracking

STONE-SPEC §9 tracks the signed-agent-receipt ecosystem without claiming
conformance: `draft-marques-asqav-compliance-receipts-07` (JCS [RFC 8785];
Ed25519 mandatory, ES256, ML-DSA-65 [FIPS 204]), SCITT [RFC 9943] (formerly
`draft-ietf-scitt-architecture`), and the house rule that a future export must
not silently rename stone-v1 chain rows. Smoke pins make draft-number drift
loud.

## Run it

```
node smoke.mjs          # 85/85 self-checks
node verify_all.mjs     # conformance run over ../ (the whole record)
```

Conformance at Task 26-b seal time: **42/42 chains verified under their own
semantics, 42/42 local-verifier agreement, 0 divergences** (11 repos, 53
jsonl files sniffed). Receipts: `experiments/outputs/receipts_e_st1.jsonl`.

# Auditor Experience — verifying a signed stone-v2 chain end-to-end

*Status: field report from the STONE-V2-PILOTS first sign pilot (Task 26-d input).
Every command below was executed for real on 2026-09-27 against the merged
sign lane (`signTip`/`verifyTipSignature`, quilt-stone#4, merge `023edbed`)
and a producer artifact generated by SuperInstance/pong-quilt's R39 pilot
(pong-quilt#51, merged `07384ac2`). Observed outputs are quoted verbatim;
nothing here is a promise. Verify by running, not by reading.*

## The artifact under audit

`checkpoints/stone-v1.signed.json` from a `node tools/prerun.js` run with
`QUILT_STONE_DIR=<quilt-stone checkout>` and `QUILT_STONE_SIGN_KEY=<producer PEM>`.
Shape: a wrapper object

```json
{ "tool": "pong-quilt", "round": "R39", "source": "...",
  "key": { "ephemeral": false, "public": "-----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----\n..." },
  "verify": { "ok": true, "tip": "ffe8abd8...", "signer": {...} },
  "chain": [ ...rows..., { "kind": "stone.sign", ... } ] }
```

Audit facts an auditor must confirm before trusting anything inside the
wrapper: the wrapper's `verify.ok` is the *producer's* self-report and is
worthless to the auditor. Only `chain` + `key.public` are inputs.

## The walk (5 checks, each observed)

```js
// auditor.mjs — zero dependencies beyond a quilt-stone checkout
import { verifyChain, verifyTipSignature } from '<quilt-stone>/stone.mjs';
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
const art = JSON.parse(readFileSync('checkpoints/stone-v1.signed.json', 'utf8'));
const rows = art.chain;
const pub = art.key.public;
```

**1. Chain integrity with the staple attached.** The `stone.sign` row is an
annotation — self-hashed against the tip, but `prev` never advances
(STONE-SPEC §4.6.1), so body verification must still pass untouched:

```
verifyChain(rows) -> {"ok":true,"alg":"stone-v1","genesis":"STONE-GENESIS-1",
  "links":6,"tip":"ffe8abd842162d717ff274fdd3c21c58622df9ede534f6b540f2ae16b69f5503", ...}
```

**2. Signature verifies against the embedded public key.**

```
verifyTipSignature(rows, pub) -> {"ok":true,"tip":"ffe8abd8...",
  "signer":{"alg":"ed25519","key_id":"pq-prerun-sign-pilot","signer_role":"producer"}}
```

**3. Negative control — body tamper.** Flip one payload byte (an `md5` field)
without touching any `row_hash`:

```
verifyChain(tampered) -> {"ok":false,"why":"hash mismatch"}
```

The hash chain catches content edits. This is necessary but NOT sufficient —
a forger with the dialect spec can re-seal and get green hashes. That is what
the staple is for.

**4. Negative control — the laundering attempt.** Tamper a body row, re-seal
with `sealChain` so every hash is green again, then copy the original
`stone.sign` row verbatim onto the forged chain. Observed:

```
verifyChain(forged)            -> {"ok":false,"why":"hash mismatch"}
verifyTipSignature(forged,pub) -> {"ok":false,"why":"signed tip does not match the chain tip (post-signature chain edit)"}
```

Both gates refuse; the signature gate names the exact reason. The signed
message is `"stone-v2" || tip_row_hash` (pinned byte-level in the sign lane's
smoke), so a re-sealed chain has a different tip and the copied staple
cannot transfer.

**5. Negative control — wrong key.** A fresh ed25519 keypair must refuse:

```
verifyTipSignature(rows, otherPub) -> {"ok":false,"why":"signature invalid for this tip and key"}
```

## Auditor experience notes (the 26-d payload)

1. **The wrapper is not evidence.** The producer self-reports `verify.ok` at
   birth; the auditor re-runs checks 1–2 from `chain` + `key.public` alone.
   A consumer that displays the wrapper's `verify` block as a checkmark is
   laundering — this is the R30 verify-before-download lesson from the
   consumer side.
2. **Key provenance is the open seam.** The pilot's ephemeral key is honestly
   labeled (`key.ephemeral: true`), but an embedded public key establishes
   only *binding*, not *identity*. Standing identity requires a key the
   auditor already trusts out-of-band (key id registry, or the IETF/SCITT
   receipt-transparency lane pinned in STONE-SPEC §9). Until then a signed
   chain proves "one key signed this tip continuously", not "Casey signed it".
3. **The two gates are complementary and both are cheap.** Hash chain =
   content continuity. Staple = continuity was signed and not re-written.
   Auditing only one gate is the failure mode the laundering control exists
   to demonstrate.
4. **Total audit cost**: one dynamic `import`, two function calls, three
   one-line mutations. Sub-second. Receipt verification at consumer side is
   not a tooling problem anymore; it is a key-distribution problem.

## Reproduction

```
git clone https://github.com/SuperInstance/quilt-stone.git
git clone https://github.com/SuperInstance/pong-quilt.git
cd pong-quilt && node tools/prerun.js   # with QUILT_STONE_DIR + QUILT_STONE_SIGN_KEY
# then run the auditor.mjs sketch above against checkpoints/stone-v1.signed.json
```
